code: int flb_parser_do(struct flb_parser *parser, const char *buf, size_t length,
note: The raw fuzz input (an LTSV record whose last field is 'CCC:t') enters the parser dispatch as buf/length.
The LTSV parser runs its packing pass over the record; the last field 'CCC:t' ends exactly at the end of the input buffer.
For the 'CCC' key (types_len != 0), the label and the 1-byte value 't' are passed to flb_parser_typecast; field points at the very end of the input buffer.

Root cause: the BOOL branch compares val with strncasecmp using a fixed length (4/5) without verifying val_len; val is not null-terminated and is only 1 byte long ('t'), so strncasecmp reads past the end of the value into the input padding/redzone.
Sink: the out-of-bounds read of val[1..3] (one to three bytes past the end of the input buffer) performed by strncasecmp.
